title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages. M_{g,ν} = π1 of the universal curve stack 𝒳_{g,ν} over Q, with base point x0. N_{g,ν} = π1(M_{g,ν,Q}, ξ0) is the arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack, an extension of Gal(Q̄/Q) by the profinite Teichmüller group T̂_{g,ν}. These sit in the exact sequence 1→π̂_{g,ν}→M_{g,ν}→N_{g,ν}→1. For a curve X of type (g,ν) over an arbitrary algebraically closed field k ⊃ Q, with point x, (13) gave a canonical isomorphism M_{X,x} ≅ M_{g,ν}, defined up to inner automorphism. Hence π_{X,x} ≅ π̂_{g,ν} up to the action of M_{g,ν}. Grothendieck called this extra structure on the profinite outer group π_{X,x} its 'canonical arithmetisation'.

This page makes that precise. First reading: the arithmetisation is a reduction of the structure group of the Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν})-torsor Isomext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π_{X,x}) to the subgroup N'_{g,ν}. Here N' is the image of N_{g,ν} under the outer representation N_{g,ν} → Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}), and 'loc' means automorphisms respecting the local (cuspidal inertia) structure.

Grothendieck then notes the epimorphism N → N' might fail to be an isomorphism. That is exactly the question of faithfulness of the outer representation: the profinite congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups on the geometric part, plus injectivity of the Galois part. So a finer formulation is needed, which works in all cases:
- (15) The right M_{g,ν}-torsor P_{X,x} = Isom in the étale fundamental groupoid of the universal curve over Q, from x0 to x. It is a torsor of étale paths.
- (16) An equivariant map P_{X,x} → Isom_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π_{X,x}), compatible with M_{g,ν} → Aut_loc(π̂_{g,ν}).
- (17) Passing to the quotient by π̂_{g,ν} gives the N_{g,ν}-torsor Q_x = path-torsor in the fundamental groupoid of M_{g,ν,Q} from ξ0 to ξ. It comes with a map Q_x → Isomext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π_{X,x}), compatible with N_{g,ν} → Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}).

He asserts that the data (16) and (17) are equivalent. This is correct because π̂_{g,ν} is centre-free in the hyperbolic case. Then M ≅ N ×_{Out} Aut and P ≅ Q ×_{Isomext} Isom, so P can be reconstructed from Q by fibre product.

Conclusion: instead of an 'extra structure' on π_{X,x}, what one has is an 'arithmetisation' in a finer sense than that given by the images P', Q'. It is an actual torsor under the abstract arithmetic group with an equivariant comparison map, not merely a subtorsor of Isomext.

Next page: pushing Q_x along N → Gal(Q̄/Q) gives the Galois torsor R_X ≅ embeddings Q̄ → k. So trivialising R_X, i.e. reducing the structure group to T̂_{g,ν}, amounts to choosing an embedding Q̄ → k.

Purpose: to define intrinsically, for curves over any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (not only over Q̄), the arithmetic structure on their profinite π1 coming from the Teichmüller tower over Q. This is groundwork for Galois–Teichmüller theory.
errors: Last compatibility line: written 'N_{g,ν} → Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π_{X,x})'. It should be Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}); the two-argument object is Isomext.
'P_{X,x}/π̂_{X,x}' mixes notations. The quotient is by the right action of π̂_{g,ν} ⊂ M_{g,ν}, or equivalently by the left action of π_{X,x}. The braces {x0},{x} denote the images in M_{g,ν}.
The claimed equivalence of (16) and (17) silently uses that π̂_{g,ν} is centre-free (true for 2g−2+ν>0). It is not stated.

ideas.what: Outer action of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{g,ν,Q} on π̂_{g,ν}, with possibly non-faithful image N'
ideas.modern_name: Galois–Teichmüller outer representation; faithfulness / profinite congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto; congruence subgroup problem: Asada, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki (g≤2)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the Galois action; an explicit doubt about injectivity is not clearly stated there

ideas.what: Torsor of étale paths P_{X,x} (from x0 to x in the universal curve over Q) with equivariant map to Isom_loc(π̂, π_{X,x}), as the 'arithmetisation' of π1 of an arbitrary curve over an arbitrary algebraically closed k ⊃ Q
ideas.modern_name: path torsors in the étale fundamental groupoid; reduction of structure group / arithmetic structure on a profinite outer group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Path-torsor viewpoint: Grothendieck SGA1, Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); arithmetic-structure viewpoint implicit in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Mochizuki)

ideas.what: Equivalence of data at the level of Aut/M versus Out/N, using the fact that a centre-free kernel makes the extension a pullback of Aut→Out
ideas.modern_name: M ≅ N ×_{Out(π̂)} Aut(π̂) for centre-free π̂
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; centre-freeness of π̂_{g,ν}: Anderson, Nakamura

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly allows that N_{g,ν} → Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}) may fail to be injective. He reformulates 'canonical arithmetisation' so that it does not depend on faithfulness, using path torsors rather than images. That faithfulness is the arithmetic congruence subgroup problem, still open for g≥3.
missed.quote: Mais si N_{g,ν} → N'_{g,ν} n'était un iso, il serait quand même plus fin de dire que via (13), on a en tous cas (15) P_{X,x} torseur à droite sous M_{g,ν}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck's awareness, around 1981, that faithfulness of the outer Teichmüller/Galois representation was not automatic. It also shows a torsor-theoretic formulation of the arithmetic structure on π1 of curves over transcendental algebraically closed fields, which is rarely formulated this way in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful foundations for Galois–Teichmüller theory: path torsors, reduction of structure group, and the centre-free Aut/Out comparison. The mathematics is largely routine given the setting. The mildly notable points are the explicit contemplation of non-faithfulness (the congruence-subgroup issue) and the torsor-based 'arithmetisation' for curves over arbitrary algebraically closed k.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads: '[restriction du groupe structural] Autext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}) dans Isomext_loc(π̂_{g,ν}, π_{X,x}), au sous-groupe ⊃ N'_{g,ν} image de N_{g,ν}'. The ∪ symbol is an inclusion sign; 'as-groupe' is 'au sous-groupe'.

'Mais si N → N' n'était un iso' carries a superscript 'épi' on the arrow, as transcribed. The next line is 'il serait quand même plus fin de dire que via (13), on a en tous cas', not 'quand = ... torseur canon'.
(15): 'torseur à droite sous M_{g,ν}'. The subscript is 'groupoïde fond. de M_{g,ν Q}'; the first letter is crossed out and possibly a script X/M, i.e. the universal curve.
The first map in (17) is crossed out and labelled '(17')' or similar; it is Aut_loc, not Autext.

Last lines: '(Au lieu d'une structure supplém. sur π_{X,x}) — c'est une "arithmétisation" en un sens plus fin que via P'_{X,x} ou Q'_x (image de P_{X,x}, Q_x)'. 'indiscernibilité' is a misreading of 'arithmétisation'.
'[-Est-ce que-]' is crossed out, then 'Les données (16) et (17) sont équivalentes.'
